newsitem.title: UK: UK's EMU option open, unlikely early member - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK's EMU option open, unlikely early member - Blair.

text.p: A Labour government would keep open Britain's option to join a European single currency, but it is highly unlikely Britain would be among the first countries to join, Labour Party leader Tony Blair said on Monday.

"The option remains open...but it is highly unlikely we'll be in the first wave and that then reduces the probability that...you'd enter in the next parliament," Blair said in an interview on BBC television.
He said it was important that Britain remained part of the negotiations because it would be affected whether it stayed in or out if European Union countries moved to monetary union.

Labour is well ahead in the opinion polls and looks set to win the May 1 election. A decision on which countries will join economic and monetary union (EMU) will be taken by early May, 1998, and a single currency is due to be launched in 1999.

Pressed to say whether the tax burden would rise under a Labour government, Blair stressed that there would be no increase in the basic or top rates of income tax, but he said he could give no commitment on the overall tax take.
"Even under Conservative proposals the tax burden is going to rise," Blair said. "Precisely for that reason, I cannot give commitments that the Labour Party can do other than that."
But he added: "There are no hidden spending commitments that require hidden taxes."
